Cheers

Is this possible somehow ?

Thanks for advices,

Grégoire

I have a data frame (example df.example with columns ref1, separation (a factor) and name) that I would like to use as a guide to build a series of checkboxInput() within a wellPanel().
Now the only solution I found is to code the different checkboxInput() in "hard":
wellPanel(
          p(strong(em(levels(df.example$separation)[1]))),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[1]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[1]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[2]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[2]), FALSE),
          p(strong(em(levels(df.example$separation)[2]))),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[3]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[3]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[4]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[4]), FALSE),
          checkboxInput(paste0("c",df.example$ref1[5]), paste0("name=", df.example$name[5]), FALSE)
)

As the data frame could change, it would be must better if I could create a dynamic version of this code but I fail to find the way to do.

Thanks a lot,

Marc

messages.subject: Re: incorporating Javascript into Shiny
messages.subject_clean: incorporating Javascript into Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I can see one issue with this line:

  plotclasses <- "($('div#plot').attr("class"))"

You're using double quotes around "class", which has the effect of breaking up the string. You probably want single quotes:

  plotclasses <- "($('div#plot').attr('class'))"

On a more general note, it's not clear from the code snippet how plotclasses is being inserted into the page, and that matters - you can't put Javascript just anywhere.

-Winston

Hi Joe,

I update apps, both on Spark and on our local shiny server, by an ssh onto the server, going into the main shiny apps folder where all the different apps are stored, and doing running a git pull from our shiny apps GitHub repo at the terminal. I always work on the apps on local repos, push to Github, and later pull down to the two servers. The only time I modify anything on the servers at the terminal is, for example, doing a touch restart.txt in an app directory, which used to trigger all files in an app to be updated in the app, but lately it seems to have no effect.

I could be wrong, but if I recall correctly, when this used to work, if I did touch restart.txt in an app directory while I had the app running in the browser, the process would stop and the browser would gray out. This no longer occurs. I hope I'm not imagining that; I think that used to be the case.

Matt

messages.body_plain:
Hi Matthew,

I'm not sure what's going on here, unfortunately. One clarification is that I think you may be mistaken about restart.txt forcefully closing connections. The way we have restart.txt setup is to leave the existing connections alone (still connected to the older process running with the older assets), but route all incoming traffic to a new process with the new code. So your old connections should continue to live on indefinitely after a restart.

I assume you're refreshing the tab with your Shiny app and still seeing the old assets? In accordance with the description above, we wouldn't expect that an existing connection would see any updates even after a restart.

Can you try clearing your browser's cache then reloading the page? And is it the server.R and UI.R files that you're updating, or some other assets in your application?

Thanks,
Jeff

Hi all,

here is a tricky question (at least for me):

I'd like to use gvisTable() with renderGvis({}) to output a matrix. I did not find a way to ask gvisTable to not remove my row names. You can see the problem on the image below and here is the code:
shiny::runApp(
list(
ui = pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("TEST"),

sidebarPanel(
helpText('This matrix does not have row names:')
),

mainPanel(
uiOutput('matrix'))
)
,
server = function(input,output){
library(googleVis)

output$matrix <- renderGvis({

matrix <- matrix(rep(1,9),nrow=3)

rownames(matrix) <- c('a','b','c')
colnames(matrix) <- c('1','2','3')

gvisTable(as.data.frame(matrix))

})
}
)
)

Obviously the following code return a matrix with row names, so this means that gvisTable removes them by default.
matrix <- matrix(rep(1,9),nrow=3)

rownames(matrix) <- c('a','b','c')
colnames(matrix) <- c('1','2','3')
matrix

Is there a way to achieve this ? Previously I was simply using renderTable({}) on the matrix, but the result is pretty ugly (R shiny: how to output a good-looking matrix using renderTable() <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/22251956/r-shiny-how-to-output-a-good-looking-matrix-using-rendertable/22253224?noredirect=1#comment33799555_22253224>)

Any advice/suggestion would be highly appreciated.

Hi Vaidotas,

All the modules Shiny Server depends on should have indeed been bundled up in the installer as you expected. So you shouldn't need to provide any npm libraries on your server in order for this to work.

In fact, I suspect that an old npm module is being found and trying to be used when we should be using the one provided in the installer.

When you uninstalled the old shiny-server package, how did you do it? We have a guide for upgrading from an old npm version (0.3.x):

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#upgrading-from-shiny-server-0.3.x

Can you try that commands we provide there?

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.subject: Embedding sliderInputs/selectInputs and radioButtons in data frame ? (Error: cannot coerce class...)
messages.subject_clean: Embedding sliderInputs/selectInputs and radioButtons in data frame ? (Error: cannot coerce class...)
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am trying to embed different types of Inputs in a matrix. It works fine for textInput() and numericInput(), but I can't find a way for selectInput(), sliderInput() and radioButton(). I would be very grateful if somebody has a solution.

I can specify the textInput and the numericInput in HTML, using something like
paste0("<input id='num", 1:2, "' class='shiny-bound-input' type='text' value=''>")

However I did not find the right way to specify the other types of inputs in HTML. For the sliders for example, I've tried
paste0("<input id='Sl_", 1:2, "' class='jslider shiny-bound-input' type = 'range' value='20' min='0' max='100'>")

but the result is not a shiny-type slider.

So I tried to use the Shiny commands:
lapply(1:2, function(i) sliderInput(inputId = paste0("sl", i), label = "", min = 0, max =100, value = 50)).

The Error that I get is: cannot coerce class ""shiny.tag"" to a data.frame. So I deduct that I should specify them in HTML -> does somebody know how to do this ?

Here is the code (and you can see the picture here below):
ui = pageWithSidebar(
headerPanel("TEST"),
  sidebarPanel(
    helpText('Some types of input can be included in a matrix and some do not')
    ),
  mainPanel(
    uiOutput('matrix_text'),
    uiOutput('matrix_num'),
    uiOutput('matrix_slider'),
    uiOutput('matrix_select'),
    uiOutput('matrix_radioButtons')
  )
)

server = function(input,output){

  output$matrix_text <- renderTable({

    matrix_input <- paste0("<input id='num", 1:2, "' class='shiny-bound-input' type='text' value=''>")
    matrix <- data.frame(matrix_input)

    row.names(matrix) <- c("r 1","r 2")
    colnames(matrix) <- c('C 1')
    matrix
  },sanitize.text.function = function(x) x)

 output$matrix_num <- renderTable({

   matrix_input <- paste0("<input id='num", 1:2, "' class='shiny-bound-input' type='number' value=''>")
   matrix <- data.frame(matrix_input)

   row.names(matrix) <- c("r 1","r 2")
   colnames(matrix) <- c('C 1')
   matrix
 },sanitize.text.function = function(x) x)

output$matrix_slider <- renderTable({

  matrix_input <- lapply(1:2, function(i) sliderInput(inputId = paste0("sl", i), label = "", min = 0, max =100, value = 50))

  matrix <- data.frame(matrix_input)

},sanitize.text.function = function(x) x)

output$matrix_select <- renderTable({

  matrix_input <- lapply(1:2, function(i) selectInput(inputId = paste0("select", i), label = "", choices = c("Cylinders" = "cyl","Transmission" = "am")))

  matrix <- data.frame(matrix_input)

},sanitize.text.function = function(x) x)

output$matrix_radioButtons <- renderTable({

  matrix_input <- lapply(1:2, function(i) radioButtons(inputId = paste0("radio", i), label = "",choices= c("Cylinders" = "cyl","Transmission" = "am"), selected = NULL))

  matrix <- data.frame(matrix_input)

},sanitize.text.function = function(x) x)

}

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))
Cheers,

ps: also posted on SO, but without answers there
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/22283095/r-shiny-how-to-embed-sliderinputs-selectinputs-and-radiobuttons-in-a-data-frame

Andrew,

I doubt that this is a conflict with shiny-server port (as long as you are not using port 8787 for shiny-server, which I don't think you are).

It might have been a problem with rstudio-server startup.

You could run this command to check your installation:  "sudo rstudio-server verify-installation"

You could also check these log files for possible errors:

/var/log/upstart/rstudio-server.log
/var/log/syslog

Also, please check for any configuration files in this location:

/etc/rstudio

If you have older files in this location (from previous installations), check to see if the content is still valid.

Hope this can help you troubleshoot the problem. Let us know how it goes.

Fereshteh

The first half of a vignette RSelenium: Driving OS/Browsers local and remote is now on Rpubs:

It details how RSelenium can be used to control browsers on a local machine.

RSelenium with local fully-fledged browsers. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1>
Firefox. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1aa>
Chrome. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1a>
Internet Explorer. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1b>
Safari. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1c>
Opera. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id1d>
RSelenium with local headless browsers. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id2>
PhantomJs. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id2a>
HtmlUnit. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id2b>
RSelenium with local mobile browsers. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id3>
Android. <http://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/13885_189d962bee6b429d86831b699967f8dd.html#id3a>
the second half will deal with controlling remote OS/browser combos on external websites and also on local websites (localhost - useful for testing a non-live app.)

Cheers

John

Andrew,

Fereshteh

make and use your own Shiny apps, you don't need Shiny Server, and I
don't recommend you worry about Shiny Server until you have figured
out how Shiny works.

The most minimal Shiny app looks like this: You make a folder (say,
"myapp") and in that folder you create a file called ui.R and another
called server.R. Make the ui.R contain this:

    shinyUI("Hello world")

And put this in server.R:

    shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    })

Then start an R session, and run these lines:

    library(shiny)
    runApp("path/to/myapp")

replacing path/to/myapp with the file path to the myapp folder. That
should automatically launch a web browser and the page should say
"Hello world". Now you should be ready to continue following the
tutorial.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server + Integrating with Apache
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server + Integrating with Apache
messages.body_plain:
1) A single R process is limited to serving a single app at a time, BUT that app is able to service many concurrent sessions (meaning, a connected browser) at once. Each session will maintain its own set of inputs and outputs. Any variables you create inside the shinyServer(function(...){ ... }) closure will be specific to a particular session.

How many sessions can you service simultaneously? That depends on how fast your hardware is, and much more significantly, how much work your application is doing. With Shiny Server Open Source edition, when you run out of capacity in your single-process-per-app, that's it. Shiny Server Pro, on the other hand, can be configured to automatically launch new processes to handle additional load.

2) Going through an iframe makes by far the most sense right now, although Shiny was designed to eventually make it possible to embed Shiny apps directly in the HTML of any web application (it's possible now, I believe, though not documented).

3) Not really. Ajax calls are inherently stateless while Shiny sessions not only maintain state, they build reactive behaviors on top of that state. This makes it easy to do partial recalculation, for example. As you make your way through the Shiny tutorial it should gradually become clear how our approach differs from the typical AJAX/RPC/REST model.

messages.subject: Shiny 0.9.0
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.9.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.9.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.8.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:

   if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')

   devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')

New Shiny Application Layout

We provided the sidebar layout and tabsets in the past. Shiny 0.9.0 introduced a few new layout and navigation functions to

make it easier to create custom page layouts using the Bootstrap grid system

provide navigation containers for creating larger applications (Navbars and Navlists)

The functions fluidRow() and column() can be used in the Bootstrap grid system to create rows and columns, respectively. The navlistPanel() function may be a good alternative to tabsetPanel(). A navlist presents the various components as a sidebar list rather than using tabs. You can see details in the new layout guide <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Shiny-Application-Layout-Guide>.

Selectize.js Integration

The JavaScript library selectize.js <https://github.com/brianreavis/selectize.js> provides a much more flexible interface compared to the basic select input. It allows us to type and search in the options, use placeholders, control the number of options/items to show/select, and so on. We have integrated selectize.js in shiny, and selectize input can be created via the new function selectizeInput(). Note the original selectInput() function uses selectize by default; you can revert back by selectInput(..., selectize = FALSE).

Please check out this example <https://demo.shinyapps.io/013-selectize/> to see a subset of features of the selectize input. There is also an example <https://demo.shinyapps.io/017-select-vs-selectize/> comparing the select and selectize input.

Enhancements of DataTables Support

We can pass literal JavaScript code via the options argument in renderDataTable() now. This makes it much easier to use DataTable plugin’s and callback functions. More DataTables options are respected on the R side, including bPaginate, iDisplayLength, bSearchable, bFilter, and so on. It is also possible to filter numeric columns with lower/upper limits.

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS file <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS>. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.

Thanks for your support -- we look forward to hearing from you!

-- The Shiny team

messages.subject: Re: data.frame error: cannot open file 'Rplots.pdf'
messages.subject_clean: data.frame error: cannot open file 'Rplots.pdf'
messages.body_plain:
I do not see the obvious problem here (perhaps you can further
simplify your example). The error about Rplots.pdf is often caused by
a plot that was not captured by your graphics device (in this case,
png()), so R tried to save it using the default pdf() device, which
writes the plot to Rplots.pdf in the current working directory, and
your app does not have write permission in the current working
directory.

BTW, I do not understand what the code below means:

png(outfile, width=600, height=425, pointsize = 10)
cplot <- function(A,B,C,D, plot=TRUE)
dev.off()

It seems you defined a function cplot() but did not really close the
png() device. It is equivalent to

png(outfile, width=600, height=425, pointsize = 10)
cplot <- function(A,B,C,D, plot=TRUE) {
  dev.off()
}

I'd recommend you to leave out the code related to renderTable() and
see if the error is still there.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
That sounds right, but just to be clear...

Shiny Server Open Source
You can only run one process per application, and R processes are single-threaded, meaning they can only do one thing at a time. So if an R operation takes 50 seconds, and you have multiple users hit your application at the same time, the first one will wait 50 seconds for their analysis to complete, the second one will wait 100 seconds (50s for the original user's computation + 50s for their own). So the last user would be waiting 500 seconds.

Shiny Server Pro
Shiny Server Pro is able to run multiple processes per application. So it can use all the cores available on your server. If you configured Shiny Server Pro to run one process per connection, and you had 10 people hit your application at once, Shiny Server Pro would spawn 10 different process, one for each user. If you had 10 cores on your server, these would all run in separate cores and each user would have their results in 50 seconds.

However, if you were running on a machine that only had one processor, then these 10 processes would all be fighting for resources. So yes, I would expect that it would take ~500 seconds for all the computation to finish. Or with two cores, it would take about 250s. Pro does allow you to control how many processes you want to spawn for any given application, so I would recommend that you aim not to spawn too many more active processes than you have cores.

Jeff

messages.subject_clean: Problem with package path with rStudio on server
messages.body_plain:
You are strongly recommended to install packages to the system-wide
library path (any one under /usr/) instead of a user's personal
library (the one under /home/). A system-wide library is shared across
all users in the OS, so its packages are guaranteed to be available.
That is not true for a personal library. You either chmod on
"/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" or run R via sudo, then install to
this library.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
TRUE is not a logical constant in JavaScript. JavaScript is not R. In
JavaScript, it is true. The condition "input.d == TRUE" should be
"input.d == true", or better, "input.d === true".

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_snippet:
TRUE is not a logical constant in JavaScript. JavaScript is not R. In
JavaScript, it is true. The condition "input.d == TRUE" should be
"input.d == true", or better, "input.d === true".

Regards,
Yihu

messages.body_plain:
In general, plot rendering is not something you want to do in a reactive expression; the reason is because reactive expressions cache their calculated values and only actually re-execute when one of the reactive inputs they depend on change. So if you are calling the same reactive that does a plot from two places in your code, then only one of those will have the behavior you want and the other will not get a plot rendered.

The changes that Stéphane recommended ensure that the "side effect free" calculations happen inside the reactive, while the operations that have side effects (printing a ggplot object) only occurs in the output and content functions where they always belong.

messages.subject: My first shiny app
messages.subject_clean: My first shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

My first shiny app:

https://opendata.shinyapps.io/Riverfly/

This app is being used to display citizen science data collected by volunteers in Glasgow, Scotland - who are monitoring river bugs and beasties. Depending on what bugs they find and their abundance it creates a 'riverfly' score.

Previously, this was data laying around in lots and lots of spreadsheets and wasn't publicly available so hopefully this makes things more engaging.

But there's a loads more improvements needed. I may switch to using googlevis or highcharts etc for the graphs. But at the moment struggling to get ggplot to display a correct legend. I'll have another look into this, but if anyone has a quick fix that would be appreciated.

I also did a bit of an ugly fix to get ggplot to generate a chart when there is only one value to plot...among other bad practices no doubt

code is here: https://github.com/fozy81/Riverfly go fork - hopefully a useful map / leaflet implementation for people to copy

...apart from the odd shiny app uploading issue (which resolved itself after a day) - shiny server has been great and most problems were my lack of R skills. The Map did take a while....

I may host this on my own server at some point (if beta ends).

thanks,

Tim

messages.body_plain:
I use a shiny app to generate a graph in SVG format in the mainpanel. Example of app is here: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/crtahlin/shinyapp_tests/

A snippet of the code that renders the mainpanel:

 mainPanel(
         tabsetPanel(
         tabPanel("Graph", h3(textOutput("message")), imageOutput("dataPlot", height="100%")),
         tabPanel("Data", tableOutput("dataTable")),
         tabPanel("Parameters", tableOutput("parametersTable")),
         tabPanel(title="Errors", verbatimTextOutput("errors")),
         tabPanel(title="Debug",h3("Client Session Parameters"), verbatimTextOutput("debug"))
       )
    )

The SVG renders, but if I move the mouse pointer over the dots on the plot, no "tooltips" are displayed. The SVG itself contains this information - if I save the plot via the right mouse button and ope it in a browser, I get the tooltips on mouse-over.

I think a general solution for displaying SVG inside webpages is described here:
http://www.w3schools.com/svg/svg_inhtml.asp

Questions:
- Is there a way to display SVG with tooltips in shiny?
- Is shiny meant to display "tooltips" in SVG (is this considered a bug)?

Thanks,
Crt

messages.body_plain:
Hi Robin,
thanks for the e-mail and the solution.
I did a solution similar your:

runApp(list(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    fileInput('inputdata', 'Input shapefile',accept=c('.shp','.dbf','.sbn','.sbx','.shx',".prj"), multiple=TRUE),

    plotOutput("SHPplot")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$SHPplot <-  renderPlot({

      myshape<- input$inputdata
      if (is.null(myshape))
        return(NULL)

    dir<-dirname(myshape[1,4])

    for ( i in 1:nrow(myshape)) {
    file.rename(myshape[i,4], paste0(dir,"/",myshape[i,1]))}

    getshp <- list.files(dir, pattern="*.shp", full.names=TRUE)
      shape<-readShapePoly(getshp)
      plot(shape)

    })
  }
))

Thanks you so much,
Best Regards
Carlos A. Silva

messages.body_plain:
Hi, You may need to read the tutorial carefully first. Here is the code:

library(XLConnect)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  Dat <- reactiveValues()
  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$iFile)) {
      inFile <- input$iFile

      wb <- loadWorkbook(inFile$datapath)
      sheets <- getSheets(wb)

      Dat$wb <- wb
      Dat$sheets <- sheets
    }
  })

  output$ui <- renderUI({
    if (!is.null(Dat$sheets)) {
      selectInput(inputId = "sheet", label = "Select a sheet:", choices = Dat$sheets)
    }
  })

  observe({
    if (!is.null(Dat$wb)) {
      if (!is.null(input$sheet)){
        dat <- readWorksheet(Dat$wb, input$sheet)
        print(names(dat))
        output$columns <- renderUI({
          checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns",
                             choices  = names(dat))
        })
      }
    }
  })
})

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  # Include css file;
  tagList(
    tags$head(

      tags$title("Upload Data"),
      tags$h1("Test")

    )
  ),

  # Control panel;
  sidebarPanel(

    fileInput(inputId = "iFile", label = "Escolha um arquivo:", accept="application/vnd.ms-excel"),

    radioButtons("model", "Escolha do Modelo:",
                 list("CRS" = "crs",
                      "VRS" = "vrs")),
    br(),

    tags$hr(),
    uiOutput(outputId = "ui"),

    uiOutput(outputId = "columns")
  ),
  # Output panel;
  mainPanel()
))

Best!

messages.subject: Re: Arranging input elements in one row
messages.subject_clean: Arranging input elements in one row
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jin Rou,

The only way I can think of to ease the pain a little is by defining a wrap.with.span function.

But of course by default the spans should sum up to 12 so the below is not right! But it serves to illustrate the idea.

Actually I usually stick to HTML ui and that is easier to set the width of the dropdowns. Currently it's quite awkward. Maybe I will try to address this with an update to ShinySky soon.

library(shiny)

wrap.with.span <- function( ...,size = rep(1,length(list(...)))) {
args <- list(...)
i <- 0
result <- lapply(args,function(a) {
i <<- i + 1
div(args[[i]],class=paste0("span",size[i]))
})
return(result)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$targetPanelExisting1 <- renderUI ({
   wellPanel(

   wrap.with.span(

   p("Q: What is the probability that "),
   selectInput("indicatorpview", "",
   choices = c("total CP" = "Total",
   "modern CP" = "Modern",
   "traditional CP" = "Traditional",
   "unmet need in FP" = "Unmet",
   "total demand in FP" = "TotalPlusUnmet",
   "demand in FP (excl modern)" = "TradPlusUnmet"
   ), selected = "total CP"),

   HTML(" in the year "),

   numericInput("yearpview", "", 2015,
    min = 1990, max = 2015, step = 1),

   HTML(" is "),

   selectInput("booleanpview", "",
   choices = c("above" = ">",
   # "at least" = ">=",
   "below" = "<"
   #, "at most" = "<="
   ), selected = "above"),
   numericInput("percInputview", "", 50,
    min = 0, max = 100, step = 1),

   HTML("%?"),
   HTML("A:"),
   strong(textOutput("postprobOutputExisting"))
                , size = c(2,3,1,2,0,3,3,1,1))
   )
  })
})

messages.subject_clean: Keeping sidebar always on the top of browser?
messages.body_plain:
Just define your own sidebarPanel with the affix class

> sidebarPanel <- function (...)
> {
> div(class = "span4", tags$form(class = "well affix", ...))
> }

To test run

> shiny::runGist("bb97d6764e3bd00c93f2")

ui.R

library(shiny)

sidebarPanel <- function (...)
{
div(class = "span4", tags$form(class = "well affix", ...))
}

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("New Application"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of observations
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("obs",
                "Number of observations:",
                min = 1,
                max = 1000,
                value = 500)
  ),

  # Show a plot of the generated distribution
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("distPlot"),
    plotOutput("distPlot1"),
    plotOutput("distPlot2"),
    plotOutput("distPlot3"),
    plotOutput("distPlot4")
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
    # number of observations
    dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
    hist(dist)

  })

  output$distPlot1 <- renderPlot({

   # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
   # number of observations
   dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
   hist(dist)

  })

  output$distPlot2 <- renderPlot({

   # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
   # number of observations
   dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
   hist(dist)

  })

  output$distPlot3 <- renderPlot({

   # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
   # number of observations
   dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
   hist(dist)

  })

  output$distPlot4 <- renderPlot({

   # generate and plot an rnorm distribution with the requested
   # number of observations
   dist <- rnorm(input$obs)
   hist(dist)

  })

})

messages.subject: How to enable user to save instances of a reactive object for later use?
messages.subject_clean: How to enable user to save instances of a reactive object for later use?
messages.body_plain:
In my shiny app I'd like to provide users with the option of saving the results of a simulation model (which is a data frame) that is dependent on a couple of inputs. The idea is to enable users to save different simulations using an action button (in the code below it is input$saveModel), have those saved simulations appear in a selectInput ui widget and then allow the users to select one or more of those saved models so that the results can be compared on a plot. The way I would like to implement this is to "stack" the data frames corresponding to all of the saved models using rbind and then filter the data frame based on the selected values in the ui widget.

Where I am running into trouble is isolating and stacking the saved models. Below is the code I have in server.R

#The results of the simulation stored as a data frame:

  prPov.df() <- reactive({ a function of user inputs })

  # The name of model that will be saved:

  currentModel <- reactive({ paste("Model", input$saveModel, sep="_") })

 # Isolating the results for future use:

  isolate({
    x <- prPov.df()
    x$Model <- currentModel()
    assign(currentModel(), x)
    .e <- environment()
    })

#Stacking the results dataframe together to "accumulate" the saved results in one object

  modelsCompare <- reactive({
    if (input$saveModel == 0) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(paste("Model", 1:input$saveModel, sep='_'), get, as.environment(.e)))
    })

My thought is that if the user clicks the action button three times (but before clicking, toggling the inputs to get different results), three data frame objects will be saved: "Model_1", "Model_2" and "Model_3". However when I run this, the console gives me an error message saying that it cannot find the object "Model_1".

As an R and shiny newbie, any support is very much appreciated.

Kind regards,

Paul

messages.body_plain:
1) Roxygen will write methods to the namespace if you have a #'@imports methods I did suggest this see post #5 ;) . There were changes in R 3.02 here are the relevant NEWS items
* R CMD check does more thorough checking of declared packages and
      namespaces.  It reports

        * packages declared in more than one of the Depends, Imports,
          Suggests and Enhances fields of the DESCRIPTION file.

        * namespaces declared in Imports but not imported from, neither
          in the NAMESPACE file nor using the :: nor ::: operators.

        * packages which are used in library() or requires() calls in
          the R code but were already put on the search path _via_
          Depends.

        * packages declared in Depends not imported _via_ the NAMESPACE
          file (except the standard packages).  Objects used from
          Depends packages should be imported to avoid conflicts and to
          allow correct operation when the namespace is loaded but not
          attached.

2) No idea to be honest it is all rather confusing

3) Some of the packages you are importing namely

    shiny,
    reshape2,
    RColorBrewer,
    rms,
    plyr

depend on methods. You are importing all of them and maybe need to be depending on some of them instead.

Josh O Brien explains it

"There is one unfortunately common exception to the advice above: if your package relies on a package A which itself "Depends" on another package B, your package will likely need to attach A with a "Depends directive.

This is because the functions in package A were written with the expectation that package B and its functions would be attached to the search() path."

from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8637993/better-explanation-of-when-to-use-imports-depends

messages.body_plain:
Dear John,

Thanks a TON! Things are making sense.

Sorry about post #5... not sure how I misread that, but thanks for sticking with me.

Best wishes,
Patrick

On Tuesday, March 18, 2014 9:00:56 PM UTC+5:30, John Harrison wrote:
> 1) Roxygen will write methods to the namespace if you have a #'@imports methods I did suggest this see post #5 ;) . There were changes in R 3.02 here are the relevant NEWS items
> * R CMD check does more thorough checking of declared packages and
>       namespaces.  It reports
>
>         * packages declared in more than one of the Depends, Imports,
>           Suggests and Enhances fields of the DESCRIPTION file.
>
>         * namespaces declared in Imports but not imported from, neither
>           in the NAMESPACE file nor using the :: nor ::: operators.
>
>         * packages which are used in library() or requires() calls in
>           the R code but were already put on the search path _via_
>           Depends.
>
>         * packages declared in Depends not imported _via_ the NAMESPACE
>           file (except the standard packages).  Objects used from
>           Depends packages should be imported to avoid conflicts and to
>           allow correct operation when the namespace is loaded but not
>           attached.
>
> 2) No idea to be honest it is all rather confusing
>
> 3) Some of the packages you are importing namely
>
>     shiny,
>     reshape2,
>     RColorBrewer,
>     rms,
>     plyr
>
> depend on methods. You are importing all of them and maybe need to be depending on some of them instead.
>
> Josh O Brien explains it
>
> "There is one unfortunately common exception to the advice above: if your package relies on a package A which itself "Depends" on another package B, your package will likely need to attach A with a "Depends directive.
>
> This is because the functions in package A were written with the expectation that package B and its functions would be attached to the search() path."
>
> from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8637993/better-explanation-of-when-to-use-imports-depends
>
> On Tuesday, March 18, 2014 10:17:33 PM UTC+7, Patrick Renschler wrote:
> > Hi John, thanks again for the help, I really appreciate it.
> >
> > That link was helpful, was the link within your link <http://obeautifulcode.com/R/How-R-Searches-And-Finds-Stuff/> .
> >
> > I've left the DESCRIPTION file as is, and I manually added import(methods) to the NAMESPACE file.
> >
> > This seems to have solved my issue. I didn't want to list all those packages as Depends and would prefer to have them as Imports.
> >
> > So this way I am avoiding the NOTE I got when I used 'Imports: methods'
> >
> > # NOTE 1:
> > * checking dependencies in R code ... NOTE
> > Namespace in Imports field not imported from: ‘methods’
> >   All declared Imports should be used.
> > See the information on DESCRIPTION files in the chapter ‘Creating R
> > packages’ of the ‘Writing R Extensions’ manual.
> >
> > And I'm avoiding the Note that I got when I used 'Depends: methods' and my NAMESPACE didn't have imports(methods):
> >
> > # NOTE 2:
> > * checking dependencies in R code ... NOTE
> > Package in Depends field not imported from: ‘methods’
> >   These packages needs to imported from for the case when
> >   this namespace is loaded but not attached.
> >
> > Despite passing R CMD check (with no errors/warnings/notes) I'm still not sure about several things:
> >
> > (1) Is roxygen not functioning properly: i.e. If I list a package as Depends, should roxygen be writing imports(package) to the NAMESPACE file? NOTE 2 and the link you sent me, suggests that you need the NAMESPACE import(methods) statement even if you have DESCRIPTION Depends: methods. My understanding is that you need the NAMESPACE import(methods) because someone might add DESCRIPTION Imports: your-package.. If that happens, then your package might not function properly because methods would not be attached, and your NAMESPACE doesn't have methods imported.
> >
> > (2) I still don't understand the error I get when I have Imports: methods. NOTE 1 above. What does it mean: Namespace in Imports field not imported from: ‘methods’. All declared Imports should be used...
> >
> > (3) I'm still not sure why I needed to include methods in the first place? The only exported function I have is:
> > webtool <- function(){
> >   shiny::runApp(system.file('webtool', package = 'pqantimalarials'))
> > }
> > and I am already stating my dependency on shiny with the statement DESCRIPTION Imports: shiny
> >
> >
> > On Tuesday, March 18, 2014 8:01:27 PM UTC+5:30, John Harrison wrote:
> > > There is useful discussion on the topic at http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/Depends-and-Imports-in-DESCRIPTION-file-td4678843.html .

messages.body_plain:
The methods package has been a forever trouble when you call pkgA::fun
in your pkgB and pkgA Imports methods. Before R core sort out the
trouble, you can make sure always load methods in your package:

  do.call(library, list('methods'))

and forget about Depends/Imports/namespace/whatever... :)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Hans,

The Admin Guide could be overwhelming since there are so many variations that you could configure your server with. I list a couple of simple scenarios here to get you started.

1) One simple configuration is to use the default configuration provided with the installation. The file is:

 /opt/shiny-server/config/default.config

You can leave it as is, or you can copy it to: /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf    (notice the name change)

With this configuration, it is assumed that your applications are in this directory: /srv/shiny-server
You don't need to create ShinyApps folder; just copy your application folder to /srv/shiny-server.

And you can access it as: http://<machine_name>:3838/<application>

2) Alternatively you can use this simple config file:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config/user-apps.config

Copy this file to: /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf

With this config file, it is assumed that applications are in ShinyApps folder in your home directory of the server:

/home/<username>/ShinyApps/<application>

So just copy your application folder to that location, and then access it as:

http://localhost:3838/<username>/<application>

Hope this helps you get further in using Shiny Server.

Fereshteh

Thanks,
Nick

Thanks for help

Xiao

If you use *xls(x)* then the first sheet will be imported. But the html code appears in the content, that is, one sees "

You can import data in csv>/em> ............." in the popup. The helpPopup() function is : helpPopup <- function(title, content, placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'), trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) { tagList( singleton( tags$head( tags$script("$(function() { $(\"[data-toggle='popover']\").popover(); })") ) ), tags$a( href = "#", `data-toggle` = "popover", # class = "btn btn-mini", title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE, `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1], `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1], tags$i(class="icon-question-sign") ) ) }

messages.subject: Re: using Shiny Server on a shared server
messages.subject_clean: using Shiny Server on a shared server
messages.body_plain:
As Huidong said, you will need root privileges to install Shiny Server.

That being said, there are hosting providers that can provide you with such an environment (often called a Virtual Private Server) -- on these you have root privileges and would be able to install Shiny Server on your machine. But in a shared hosting environment like the one you describe, you would not be able to set it up.

Some of the names to look at if you want to get into your own virtual server:
Amazon AWS <http://aws.amazon.com/ec2/> - The most popular choice right now, but they can be a little pricey.
DigitalOcean <https://www.digitalocean.com/> - They're relatively new, but have a much lower entry point
Dreamhost <http://www.dreamhost.com/>, GoDaddy, etc. (maybe even Bluehost, I'm unfamiliar with them) - In addition to the default "shared" hosting environments, many of these companies offer Virtual Private Servers for an additional fee on which you'd have root privileges.

One final option to keep in mind if you'd rather not manage your own server is our hosted service, http://shinyapps.io/. This service will manage the server for you and allow you to focus just on developing your Shiny Applications. It's currently in Alpha testing and is free for the time being.

Jeff

What system are you using to host your Virtual Machine? VMWare? VirtualBox?

Most of these systems have a way to map folders on your "host" (Windows) to your "guest" (Ubuntu). Here's an example: https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch04.html#sharedfolders

The simplest way may be to just the files to the Ubuntu guest as if it were a remote server. You could use an SFTP client on your Windows machine to send files to a remote Linux machine (even if it happens to be a VM running on your local box). You'd just need to make sure the appropriate ports are open and the necessary services are running on your Ubuntu machine. But I'm sure Google is riddled with help for that problem depending on what virtualization system you're using.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server app hosting
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server app hosting
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

There are various ways to get your applications accessible on the VM, one way is to share folders between your host and your VM. You can find information online on how to share folders. I have some of my folders on the host machine mounted in /mnt/hgfs directory of my VM.

Shiny Server would be able to process your applications as long as 1) the files are accessible on the VM file system 2) and you specify in the configuration file where to locate your applications.

Let's take the simple case of using Shiny example applications to be served by the server. Please refer to this section of the latest Shiny Server Admin Guide <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#host-a-directory-of-applications-1> for steps on finding location of the example applications on your server machine, and copying one example to /srv/shiny-server folder.
When the application folder has been copied here, assuming you are using the default configuration file of Shiny Server, you should be able to access the applications at http://localhost:3838/01_hello

Then you can follow the same pattern for your own applications:
- Have the applications in a folder accessible on the VM,
- and specify the path to this folder in "site_dir" directive of your Shiny Server configuration file.

There are other methods of hosting your applications which you can read in the Admin Guide. I just listed one above.

For the case of running applications locally using runApp() command, you have to make sure you provide the correct path to the application folder. As the guide suggests, use this command:
R -e "system.file('examples/01_hello', package='shiny')"
to locate the example application on your system, and then use that path with your runApp() command. For example:
runApp("/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/shiny/examples/01_hello/")

Hope this helps to get you started. And let us know if you have more issues.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server app hosting
messages.subject_clean: Shiny server app hosting
messages.body_plain:
It looks like you're having an issue creating a log file for an application. These get created automatically for you when a Shiny app starts. But if the user running Shiny doesn't have permissions to create a file in the log directory, you might get an error.

What are the permissions on your Shiny log directory? (`ls -l /var/log/shiny-server`)
What user are you running Shiny Server as? (i.e. by default it will be started by root on startup. Are you running it yourself manually by calling "shiny-server" from the command line? If so, if will be running as the user you are when you execute that command.)

You need to make sure that the user you're running shiny-server as has appropriate permissions to /var/log/shiny-server and all of the parent directories (/var/log/ and /var/).

Jeff

I can alter our code to work in spite of this error and release a new version of our package, but if you think you are likely to release a new version of shiny that overcomes the error in question in the next couple of days, that would seem to be poor practice on my part.

Would you be able to give us an estimate on when we can expect a new version of shiny to come out?

Thanks in advance. And keep up the great work on shiny (it's excellent)!

Cheers,
Caitlin.

messages.subject: Summer internships available at Novartis Pharmaceuticals Advanced Quantitative Sciences group
messages.subject_clean: Summer internships available at Novartis Pharmaceuticals Advanced Quantitative Sciences group
messages.body_plain:
Dear R Users,

I want to call attention to internships in my group at Novartis Pharmaceuticals’ Advanced Quantitative Sciences group.
For at least one of these, we're looking for deployment of mathematical models in R, and development of apps in Shiny. More details below, and on our website.

I. Decision support platform and model library
Develop/implement a library of decision support models and dynamic visualizations within a web-based “dashboard” decision support platform.
Requirements: Facility with mathematical modeling, R/Shiny and Javascript/Jquery. Skills in PHP, Python, relational databases, and Linux shell scripting are also desirable.

II. Web-based user interface for clinical trial design and dose regimen exploration
Implement a web-based user interface for communicating model results with clinicians:
a. comparing clinical trial designs and outcomes
b. exploring dose regimens by integrating existing knowledge and uncertainties
Requirement: Hands-on experience in Python and libraries related to data processing/analysis, user-interface design and web development. Working experience with R is a plus

III. Bayesian pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD)
a. Develop a core library of Bayesian PK/PD models in the Stan (http://mc-stan.org) modeling language to support the development of drug-disease models.
b. Using this library, extend an existing visual acuity model among age-related macular degeneration (AMD) patients treated with anti-VEGF therapy.
Requirements: Strong computing and statistical inference/modeling background, including R and C/C++ experience (ideally already familiar with Stan).

IV. Automated dataset processing
Build an automated tool to process clinical datasets with associated metadata into appropriate structure, documentation and tracking databases, along with associated test datasets for model simulation.
Requirements: Experienced with SAS, databases, and Linux

V. Mechanistic disease modeling
a. Implement an existing model of blood pressure regulation and renal function for sharing with external groups through the Drug Disease Model Resources consortium – an industry-academic consortium that aims to build and maintain a universally applicable, open source, model based framework for modeling and simulation.
b. Implement and evaluate a semi-mechanistic model for diabetes markers
Requirements: Biomedical engineering, systems biology, or related field, with some modeling experience. Experience with Matlab and/or NONMEM.

All interns must be thorough, committed to completion, and willing to rapidly learn tools as needed to get the job done.
How to Apply
Students should please apply for intern positions directly online at http://www.novartis.com/careers/job-search/index.shtml#division=Pharma (Search for 139591BR, additional requirements listed on website)

messages.body_plain:
Just an update... I tried to finish each run through the loop with a shiny:::flushReact(), but this did not help... It is still only the last result that gets send...

The question can actually be boiled down to a very general use case: How can you set up a reactive function containing a loop where the result of each iteration needs to be passed on. Another use case for this is progress bars...

best

Thomas

Den onsdag den 26. marts 2014 15.18.08 UTC+1 skrev Thomas Lin Pedersen:
> Hi
>
> I'm developing a shiny app that lets the user upload a set of files and perform an analysis on each of them. The result of the analysis is then send back to the user with a custom shiny output. Because the size of the analysis result is rather big, I want to send it for each analysis separately, instead of pooling everything together.
>
> I'm having trouble with getting this to work as I cannot find a way to halt my for loop until the result has been send. To illustrate my approach here is some pseudo code:
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>     dataAdded <- reactiveValues(counter=0)
>     dataStore <- list()
>
>     dataGenerator <- observe({
>         if(input$analysisButton == 0) return(c())
>
>         files <- isolate({input$datafiles})
>
>         for(i in files) {
>             result <- doExpensiveAnalysis(i)
>             index <- length(dataStore)+1
>             dataStore[[index]] <<- result
>             dataAdded$counter <<- isolate(dataAdded$counter)+1
>         }
>     })
>     data <- reactive({
>         index <- dataAdded$counter
>         if(index != 0) {
>             do.call('renderData', dataStore[[length(dataStore)]])
>         }
>     })
>     output$result <- reactive({data()})
> }
>
> While this might be the wrong approach, the main idea is this: On the server there is a variable (dataStore) holding on to the results in a list. An observer depends on a button and when executing, loops through the files, analyse them, adds them to the dataStore and notifies the server that the dataStore has been updated by elevating the reactive value dataAdded$counter by one. Another reactive expression depends on the dataAdded$counter and reads the last value of the dataStore, do some preprocessing and sets it to the client (via output$result).
>
> The problem is that data() is not evaluated each time data$Added$counter is increased, but only once the for-loop in dataGenerator is completed. The result of this is that only the result of the last analysis is ever sent to the client.
>
> Is there a way to force evaluation of a reactive expression within another function? or is there a better setup than this that achieves the same thing?
>
> best
>
> Thomas

messages.subject: Re: centos AWS shiny and rstudio install instructions
messages.subject_clean: centos AWS shiny and rstudio install instructions
messages.body_plain:
You'll want to check a few things if you can't get in to the server.

The Shiny Server log at /var/log/shiny-server.log If Shiny Server is having problems, they'll be listed here. If everything looks ok here, then it's most likely not a Shiny Server issue.
For Amazon AWS, you'll want to check the security group your instance is running in to make sure that port 3838 is open and available.
Some distributions ship with a firewall like iptables enabled by default. You'll need to be sure that port 3838 isn't being blocked by your machine.

If none of those work, is SELinux enabled on your machine?

Jeff

  sliderInput("speed",label="Speed",min=0,max=25,value=15),

))

server.R

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input,output) {

  predictModel <- reactive({
    a <- lm(dist ~ speed,data=cars)

    predict(a,data.frame(speed = c(1,input$speed,25)))

  output$model <- renderDataTable({

    d = data.frame(mile = as.vector(predictModel()))

  })
})

messages.subject: Re: Halt execution of function until all observers are validated
messages.subject_clean: Halt execution of function until all observers are validated
messages.body_plain:
I got this solved by changing the code up and using invalidateLater. The new structure is roughly:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    dataAdded <- reactiveValues(counter=0)
    dataStore <- list()

    dataFiles <- c()
    analysisButtonCount <- 0

    dataGenerator <- observe({
        if(input$analysisButton == 0) return(c())

        if(input$analysisButton != analysisButtonCount) {
            dataFiles <<- isolate({input$datafiles})
            analysisButtonCount <<- input$analysisButton
        }

        result <- doExpensiveAnalysis(dataFiles[1])
        index <- length(dataStore)+1
        dataStore[[index]] <<- list(
            name=basename(dataFiles[1]),
            mzID=res,
            mzML=raw
            )
        dataFiles <<- dataFiles[-1]
        dataAdded$counter <<- isolate(dataAdded$counter)+1

        if(length(dataFiles)) {
            invalidateLater(1, session)
        }

    })
    data <- reactive({
        index <- dataAdded$counter
        if(index != 0) {
            do.call('renderData', dataStore[[length(dataStore)]])
        }
    })
    output$result <- reactive({data()})

}

messages.subject: Re: Color dataframe cells in R shiny
messages.subject_clean: Color dataframe cells in R shiny
messages.body_plain:
Please Marta don't crosspost on SO <http://stackoverflow.com/q/22684162/1100107> without mentioning you do it.

I paste my answer below for further discussion.

library(pander)
library(markdown)
library(stringr)
library(shiny)

# function derived from the highlightHTMLcells() function of the highlightHTML package
colortable <- function(htmltab, css, style="table-condensed table-bordered"){
  tmp <- str_split(htmltab, "\n")[[1]]
  CSSid <- gsub("\\{.+", "", css)
  CSSid <- gsub("^[\\s+]|\\s+$", "", CSSid)
  CSSidPaste <- gsub("#", "", CSSid)
  CSSid2 <- paste(" ", CSSid, sep = "")
  ids <- paste0("<td id='", CSSidPaste, "'")
  for (i in 1:length(CSSid)) {
    locations <- grep(CSSid[i], tmp)
    tmp[locations] <- gsub("<td", ids[i], tmp[locations])
    tmp[locations] <- gsub(CSSid2[i], "", tmp[locations],
                           fixed = TRUE)
  }
  htmltab <- paste(tmp, collapse="\n")
  Encoding(htmltab) <- "UTF-8"
  list(
    tags$style(type="text/css", paste(css, collapse="\n")),
    tags$script(sprintf(
                  '$( "table" ).addClass( "table %s" );', style
                )),
    HTML(htmltab)
  )
}

##
runApp(
  list(
    ui=pageWithSidebar(
      headerPanel(""),
      sidebarPanel(
      ),
      mainPanel(
        uiOutput("htmltable")
      )
    ),
    server=function(input,output,session){
      output$htmltable <- renderUI({
        # define CSS tags
        css <- c("#bgred {background-color: #FF0000;}",
                 "#bgblue {background-color: #0000FF;}")
        # example data frame
        # add the tag inside the cells
        tab <- data.frame(x=c("A","B"), y=c("red cell #bgred", "blue cell #bgblue"))
        # generate html table with pander package and markdown package
        htmltab <- markdownToHTML(
          text=pandoc.table.return(
            tab,
            style="rmarkdown", split.tables=Inf
          ),
          fragment.only=TRUE
        )
        colortable(htmltab, css)
      })
    })
)

On Thursday, March 27, 2014 4:00:33 PM UTC-5, Stéphane Laurent wrote:
> Please Marta don't crosspost on SO <http://stackoverflow.com/q/22684162/1100107> without mentioning you do it.
>
> I paste my answer below for further discussion.
>
>
> library(pander)
> library(markdown)
> library(stringr)
> library(shiny)
>
> # function derived from the highlightHTMLcells() function of the highlightHTML package
> colortable <- function(htmltab, css, style="table-condensed table-bordered"){
>   tmp <- str_split(htmltab, "\n")[[1]]
>   CSSid <- gsub("\\{.+", "", css)
>   CSSid <- gsub("^[\\s+]|\\s+$", "", CSSid)
>   CSSidPaste <- gsub("#", "", CSSid)
>   CSSid2 <- paste(" ", CSSid, sep = "")
>   ids <- paste0("<td id='", CSSidPaste, "'")
>   for (i in 1:length(CSSid)) {
>     locations <- grep(CSSid[i], tmp)
>     tmp[locations] <- gsub("<td", ids[i], tmp[locations])
>     tmp[locations] <- gsub(CSSid2[i], "", tmp[locations],
>                            fixed = TRUE)
>   }
>   htmltab <- paste(tmp, collapse="\n")
>   Encoding(htmltab) <- "UTF-8"
>   list(
>     tags$style(type="text/css", paste(css, collapse="\n")),
>     tags$script(sprintf(
>                   '$( "table" ).addClass( "table %s" );', style
>                 )),
>     HTML(htmltab)
>   )
> }
>
> ##
> runApp(
>   list(
>     ui=pageWithSidebar(
>       headerPanel(""),
>       sidebarPanel(
>       ),
>       mainPanel(
>         uiOutput("htmltable")
>       )
>     ),
>     server=function(input,output,session){
>       output$htmltable <- renderUI({
>         # define CSS tags
>         css <- c("#bgred {background-color: #FF0000;}",
>                  "#bgblue {background-color: #0000FF;}")
>         # example data frame
>         # add the tag inside the cells
>         tab <- data.frame(x=c("A","B"), y=c("red cell #bgred", "blue cell #bgblue"))
>         # generate html table with pander package and markdown package
>         htmltab <- markdownToHTML(
>           text=pandoc.table.return(
>             tab,
>             style="rmarkdown", split.tables=Inf
>           ),
>           fragment.only=TRUE
>         )
>         colortable(htmltab, css)
>       })
>     })
> )
>

Thank you Jeff. Below is the "list" version of your example, for a quicker trying. library(shiny) library(shinyTable) runApp( list( ui=pageWithSidebar( # Application title headerPanel("Simple Shiny Table!"), sidebarPanel( #sliderInput("slider", "Number of rows:", 1, 26, 5), #HTML("
"), helpText(HTML("A simple table with validation. The first column must be a number and if it's >= 100, it will be assigned the value of 99. Other columns can be anything. Additionally, the second column has server-side styling applied and will highlight as 'invalid' any value >= 100, and will 'warn' on values >= 50.

Created using ">shinyTable.")) ), # Show the simple table mainPanel( htable("tbl", headers="provided") ) ), server=function(input,output,session){ cachedTbl <- NULL validate <- function(tbl){ updateTableStyle(session, "tbl", "valid", which(as.numeric(tbl$num2) < 50), 2) updateTableStyle(session, "tbl", "warning", which(as.numeric(tbl$num2) >= 50 & as.numeric(tbl$num2) < 100), 2) updateTableStyle(session, "tbl", "invalid", which(as.numeric(tbl$num2) >= 100), 2) } output$tbl <- renderHtable({ if (is.null(input$tbl)){ rows <- 5 # Seed the element with some data initially tbl <- data.frame(list(num1=1:rows, num2=(1:rows)*20, letter=LETTERS[1:(rows)])) validate(tbl) cachedTbl <<- tbl return(tbl) } else{ # Updates from client. The server has been made aware and can do some # validation or updates here, then send back the revised table. In this # case, we'll filter any number >= 100 in the first column. tbl <- input$tbl # Any non-numeric data should be replaced with the cached data. tbl[is.na (as.integer(as.character(tbl[,1]))),1] <- as.character(cachedTbl[is.na (as.integer(as.character(tbl[,1]))),1]) validate(tbl) tbl[as.integer(as.character(tbl[,1])) >= 100,1] <- 99 cachedTbl <<- tbl return(tbl) } }) }) )

messages.subject: New Shiny website launched; Shiny 0.9 released
messages.subject_clean: New Shiny website launched; Shiny 0.9 released
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, we blogged about this yesterday but I totally forgot to post it here as well. Included below is the content of the blog post <http://blog.rstudio.org/2014/03/27/shiny-website-and-0-9/>.

We’re excited to introduce to you our new website for Shiny: shiny.rstudio.com <http://shiny.rstudio.com/>!

 <http://shiny.rstudio.com/>

We’ve included articles <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/> on many Shiny-related topics, dozens of example applications <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/>, and an all-new tutorial <http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/> for getting started.

Whether you’re a beginner or expert at Shiny, we hope that having these resources available in one place will help you find the information you need.

We’d also like to announce Shiny 0.9, now available on CRAN. This release includes many bug fixes and new features, including:
New application layout options

Until now, the vast majority of Shiny apps have used a sidebar-style layout. Shiny 0.9 introduces new layout features to:
Make it easy to create custom page layouts using the Bootstrap grid system. See our new application layout guide <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/layout-guide.html> or a live example <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/plot-plus-three-columns.html>.
Provide navigation bars and lists for separating your application into different pages. See navbarPage <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/navbarPage.html> and navlistPanel <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/navlistPanel.html>, and this example <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/navbar-example.html>.
Enhance tabsetPanel <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/navlistPanel.html> to allow pill-style tabs, and to let tabs be placed above, below, or to either side of tab content.
Create floating panels and place them relative to the sides of the page, optionally making them draggable. See absolutePanel <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/absolutePanel.html> or this example <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/absolutely-positioned-panels.html>.
Use Bootstrap themes <https://www.google.com/webhp?ion=1&espv=2&ie=UTF-8#q=bootstrap+themes> to easily modify the fonts and colors of your application.Example <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/retirement-simulation.html>

You can see many of these features in action together in our reimplementation <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/superzip-example.html> of the Washington Post’s interactive article on Super Zips <http://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/local/2013/11/09/washington-a-world-apart/>.
Selectize.js integration

The JavaScript library selectize.js <https://github.com/brianreavis/selectize.js> provides a much more flexible interface compared to the basic select input. It allows you to type and search in the options, use placeholders, control the number of options/items to show/select, and so on.

We have integrated selectize.js in shiny 0.9, and selectInput now creates selectize inputs by default. (You can revert back to plain select inputs by passingselectize=FALSE to selectInput.) For more advanced uses, we have included a new selectizeInput function that lets you pass options to selectize.

Please check out this example <https://demo.shinyapps.io/013-selectize/> to see a subset of features of the selectize input. There is also an example <https://demo.shinyapps.io/017-select-vs-selectize/> comparing the select and selectize input.
Showcase mode

Shiny apps can now (optionally) run in a “showcase” mode in which the app’s R code can be automatically displayed within the app. Most of the Shiny example apps in our newgallery <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/> use showcase mode.

 <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/kmeans-example.html>

As you interact with the application, reactive expressions and outputs in server.R will light up as they execute. This can be helpful in visualizing the reactivity in your app.

See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/display-modes.html> to learn more.

As always, you can install the latest release of Shiny by running this command at the R console:

install.packages("shiny")

The complete list of bug fixes and features is available in the NEWS file <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/NEWS>.

We hope you’ll find these new features helpful in exploring and understanding your data!

messages.subject: Re: refreshing highcharts in shiny
messages.subject_clean: refreshing highcharts in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Here's some example code.  In shiny, when clicking on Joe, the plot won't redraw itself.  However, clicking on all 4 values in the legend and then adding one back will force it to redraw.  I'm running rCharts 0.4.2 and shiny 0.9.1.

If you drop out of shiny and then plot local_a, then you can click on Joe in the viewer and the plot redraws itself nicely.

Anyone else experienced this behavior?

## ui.R
require(shiny)
require(rCharts)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("rCharts"),
  sidebarPanel(
  ),
  mainPanel(
    chartOutput("myChart", "highcharts")
  )
))

## server.R
require(shiny)
require(rCharts)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$myChart <- renderChart2({

    df <- data.frame(
      name = c("John", "John", "Joe", "Joe", "Jane", "Jane", "Janet", "Janet"),
      data = sample(1:10, 8, replace = T),
      stack = c(rep("male", 4), rep("female", 4))
    )

    a <- rCharts:::Highcharts$new()

    a$chart(type = "column")
    a$plotOptions(column = list(stacking = "normal"))
    a$xAxis(categories = c("Apples", "Oranges"))

    # a$series(name = "John", data = c(5, 3), stack = "male")
    # a$series(name = "Joe", data = c(3, 4), stack = "male")
    # a$series(name = "Jane", data = c(2, 5), stack = "female")
    # a$series(name = "Janet", data = c(3, 1), stack = "female")

    invisible(sapply(unique(df$name), function(name){
      d <- df[df$name == name, ]
      a$series(name = name, data = d$data, stack = d$stack[[1]])
    }))

    local_a <<- a
    return(a)
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: Leaflet in R Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Leaflet in R Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I also struggled to get polygons to work. I have a data.frame with columns lat.start, lng.start, lat.end, lng.end, Count and I wanted to add a line to the map for each row of the data.frame. Here is the code that works:
    for (i in 1:nrow(uniqueTotals))
      bikeMap$addPolygon(c(uniqueTotals$lat.start[i], uniqueTotals$lat.end[i], 0),
                     c(uniqueTotals$lng.start[i], uniqueTotals$lng.end[i], 0),
                     layerId=list(as.character(i)),
                     options=list(list(weight=uniqueTotals$Count[i])))

A couple of things to note:
The last point of the polygon is not used, so I added an extra 0 point at the end. This may be a bug in bindings.js where it pops the last point before calling L.polygon().
layerId must be a list even though it has only one element; otherwise bindings.js uses *characters* of layerId as the actual id, so it just uses the first character and only 10 lines plot.
options has to be a list of lists.

messages.subject: Re: shiny integration with other JS frameworks
messages.subject_clean: shiny integration with other JS frameworks
messages.body_plain:
I don't think anyone has tried it, but my suspicion is that it should mostly work. I'm not sure if it will make things easier though, it may make things harder and more confusing.

The main thing is that Shiny needs to be notified before and after you modify the DOM if there's the possibility of Shiny inputs/outputs being inside the parts of the DOM you're changing. Assume that "scope" is a DOM node whose children you're about to mess with (you can even use the document object if you want):

Shiny.unbindAll(scope);
// Make changes to the DOM here
Shiny.bindAll(scope);

Also I can't guarantee that these APIs won't change in the future, they're not (yet) part of the officially supported API. That said, they haven't changed in quite a while.

messages.subject: Re: updating global variables
messages.subject_clean: updating global variables
messages.body_plain:
Replace the declaration of obj with this:

values <- reactiveValues(obj = read.csv("file"))

And anytime you want to read/write the variable, refer to values$obj. The reactiveValues function creates a new list-like object on which you can store named values; reads and writes to these named values are reactive-aware.

The way you were doing it doesn't work because "obj" is just a normal, non-reactive variable; Shiny's reactive framework only knows when reactive things change. Inputs and reactive expressions both fall into this category.

The other possibility is a new feature introduced in Shiny 0.9 called "makeReactiveBinding"; just leave your code as it is in your email, and add the line "makeReactiveBinding(obj)" right before the declaration of obj. That will let you use obj as if it is a normal variable, but it's actually a reactive variable. I haven't decided if this is actually a good idea or not (as it's not obvious from looking at a read/write of this variable that anything out of the ordinary is going on), if you want you can give it a try and let me know whether it helps or hurts vs. the reactiveValues approach.
